decisions.reason: After two years this rye country bread looks like a low-cost, close-to-core item, so unless sales are clearly weak it remains worth keeping in the assortment.
The seeded rye mixed bread fits the core range well and is cheap to continue, with enough mainstream appeal to justify keeping it open as an option.
By now the niche malt profile and overlap with several other rye launches likely reveal limited incremental value, so rationalizing it is the better use of capacity.
As a classic seasonal marzipan variant in a German bakery-confectionery business, it is still a sensible stollen option to retain absent clear failure signals.
The ancient grain bread remains a differentiated artisanal product with some upside, and its higher demand uncertainty is still outweighed by manageable continuation costs.
